prompt.context: Our client is a start-up with the ability to deliver broadband internet to commercial airlines.
prompt.question: How would you help them think about their offering?

clarifying_info.a: The start-up would charge customers on a per-flight pricing model.

clarifying_info.q: How much up-front investment is required?
clarifying_info.a: The company would have to invest relatively little up front and would keep most of the revenues.

clarifying_info.q: How many planes are in the market?
What revenue is needed per plane to be profitable?
clarifying_info.a: The company has discovered that if they can generate $250,000 per plane in annual revenue, they will be profitable installing the technology on that plane.

exhibits.title: Airline Passenger Breakdown
exhibits.shows: A table showing seat counts and load factors by cabin class (First and Coach) used to estimate total laptop users per plane per leg
exhibits.data: First class: 20 seats, 0.75 load factor; Coach: 180 seats, 0.75 load factor; Business traveler share: 100% (First), 30% (Coach)

exhibits.title: Price vs. Penetration Combinations
exhibits.shows: A table or chart showing various price points and the corresponding number of users per 100 passengers, used to determine optimal pricing
exhibits.data: $5 -> 30 users; $10 -> 25 users; $15 -> 20 users; $20 -> 10 users; $25 -> 5 users (per 100 passengers)

framework: Industry & Market Analysis: size of the broadband-on-airlines market, growth trends, customer segments (business vs. leisure travelers)
Competitive Landscape: existing or potential competitors, intellectual property position, low-speed vs. high-speed alternatives
Customer Value Proposition: willingness to pay, usage patterns, demand by cabin class
Financial Feasibility: market size calculation, pricing optimization, break-even analysis
Risks & Mitigations: technology, regulatory, adoption, competitive IP threats

questions.prompt: Estimate the annual potential market (total user-legs per year)
questions.guidance: Candidate should use the Exhibit 1 data to calculate laptop users per plane, then scale by fleet size and annual flight legs. Key steps: compute full seats (seats x load factor), apply business traveler share to get laptop users by class, sum across classes, multiply by planes and legs per year.

math.setup: First: 20 seats x 0.75 = 15 full seats x 100% biz = 15 laptop users. Coach: 180 seats x 0.75 = 135 full seats x 30% biz = 40.5 laptop users. Total per plane per leg: 15 + 40.5 = ~55.5 (~50 rounded). Annual legs per plane: 2,000.
steps: 15 (First) + 40.5 (Coach) = 55.5 laptop users per plane per leg
Round to ~50 laptop users per plane per leg
3,000 planes x 2,000 legs/plane x 50 laptop users/leg = 300,000,000 user-legs per year

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, determine the optimal price per flight to maximize revenue per leg
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate revenue per flight at each price point (price x users) and identify the maximum. The optimal price maximizes total revenue per flight.

math.setup: Assume 100 passengers per flight. Revenue = price x number of users at that price.
math.answer: Optimal price = $15/flight (maximizes revenue at $300 per flight per 100 passengers)

questions.prompt: Calculate the break-even number of users per leg, and determine whether the business will break even given the pricing and adoption assumptions
questions.guidance: Candidate should divide the required annual revenue per plane by annual legs to get required revenue per leg, then divide by price to find required users per leg. Compare to estimated users at the chosen price point.

math.setup: Required annual revenue per plane = $250,000. Annual legs per plane = 2,000. Price = $15.
steps: $125 / $15 per user = ~8.3 users needed per leg to break even
At $15, penetration rate is 20% (20 users per 100 passengers); with ~50 laptop users per leg, estimated paying users = 50 x 20% = 10 users per leg
math.answer: Break-even requires ~8 users/leg; estimated demand is ~10 users/leg at $15. Yes, the company should break even.

brainstorming.prompt: What risks are associated with this business model?

categories.name: Competitive / IP Risks
ideas: Competitors developing low-speed internet alternatives at lower price
Patent challenges or expiration eroding the high-speed monopoly
Large telecom players entering the space with more capital

categories.name: Adoption / Demand Risks
ideas: Slower-than-expected passenger adoption of in-flight internet
Leisure travelers unwilling to pay, leaving only business travelers
Shift to mobile data making laptop-based Wi-Fi less relevant

categories.name: Technology / Operational Risks
ideas: Integration costs with airline IT systems varying widely

categories.name: Airline Partner Risks
ideas: Airlines demanding higher revenue share, compressing margins
Airline bankruptcies or fleet reductions shrinking addressable market

recommendation: Enter the market: the break-even analysis shows that at $15/flight the company exceeds the ~8 users/leg threshold needed for profitability, with an estimated 10 users/leg
The total addressable market is large (~300M user-legs/year), and the company holds the patent on high-speed connections, providing a meaningful competitive moat
Relatively low up-front investment required further supports entry
risks: Low-speed internet alternatives from competitors could undercut demand
Adoption risk if business travelers are price-sensitive or if airlines resist installation
next_steps: Prioritize airlines with high business-traveler load factors (e.g., major hub-to-hub routes) to maximize early adoption
Monitor competitive developments in low-speed connectivity and reinforce IP position
Track actual penetration rates per leg versus the 20% assumption and adjust pricing accordingly
